staffing_plan.notes: Owns scope sign-off (T1), vendor selection (T3), internal demo (T16), UAT coordination (T24), documentation (T27), adoption planning (T28), post-launch ownership (T29), go-live sign-off (T32). Full-time across all phases. Single point of accountability for backlog prioritization and trade-off decisions per R5 mitigation.

Owns architecture design (T4), Workday API validation (T6), Azure AD SSO (T7), e-signature integration (T10), Workday data pre-population (T11), Azure AD account provisioning (T12), audit logging (T15), error handling/retry logic (T17), security review/SOC 2 controls (T19), bug resolution (T26), production deployment (T30). Critical path tasks T4, T6, T7, T10, T11, T12, T15, T17, T19. Must be full-time and dedicated; no competing priorities per R8 mitigation. Allocation 53.1% reflects 276h / 520h total project hours.

Owns UI wireframes (T5), portal UI shell (T8), onboarding checklist UI (T9), team introduction feature (T13), HR admin dashboard (T14), form validation/edge cases (T18), accessibility audit/remediation (T25). Critical path tasks T5, T8, T9, T13, T14, T18. Must be full-time through Phase 4; no competing priorities per R8 mitigation. Allocation 28.1% reflects 146h / 520h total project hours.

Owns user personas and success metrics (T2), detailed wireframes and user flows (T5). Front-loaded to Phase 1-2 per benchmark. Critical path tasks T2, T5. Allocation 10.8% reflects 56h / 520h total project hours. Can transition to 20-30% allocation on other projects after Phase 2 completion.

Owns end-to-end integration testing (T20), automated test suite (T22), UAT execution (T24), accessibility audit (T25), smoke testing in production (T31). Critical path task T20. QA effort 128h / (276h Backend + 146h Frontend) = 128h / 422h dev hours = 30.3%, exceeds 25% minimum per PMBOK 8.2. Allocation 24.6% reflects 128h / 520h total project hours. Back-loaded to Phase 3-5 per benchmark.
Owns production deployment (T30). Back-loaded to Phase 5 per benchmark. Allocation 3.1% reflects 16h / 520h total project hours. Can be part-time or shared resource; not on critical path.

Supports Azure AD provisioning proof-of-concept (Phase 1), validates SCIM support for SaaS tools (Phase 1), pairs with Backend Developer on automation scripting (Phase 2), validates provisioning workflow (Phase 2). Not a dedicated project role but critical stakeholder per R2 mitigation. Allocation 6.9% reflects 36h / 520h total project hours. Assumes 10-15% of IT Administrator's time over 26 weeks.

open_questions.question: Is the e-signature service (UC2) already selected with API documentation available, or does vendor evaluation and legal compliance review need to occur in Phase 1? This directly impacts T3 duration and Phase 1 timeline.
open_questions.impact_if_unanswered: If not selected, Phase 1 extends 1–2 weeks for vendor evaluation and legal review; if forms require redesign, Phase 2 extends 1–3 weeks. Assumption A3 risk_if_wrong = MEDIUM; staffing plan assumes selection is complete by Phase 1 week 2.

open_questions.question: What is the complete scope of IT account provisioning (UC4): email-only, or does it include Slack, SaaS tools, and VPN access? Which specific SaaS tools require provisioning?
open_questions.impact_if_unanswered: Scope creep on integrations directly impacts Phase 2 timeline (T12 effort estimate assumes email + Slack + configured SaaS tools). Undefined SaaS tool list may require re-scoping or delay. Risk R4 probability = MEDIUM, impact = HIGH.

open_questions.question: Does Workday API integration require custom field mapping, custom configuration, or is standard employee data export sufficient for pre-population? Is sandbox access confirmed and stable?
open_questions.impact_if_unanswered: If custom configuration required, Phase 2 integration work (T6, T11) extends 2–4 weeks. Assumption A1 risk_if_wrong = HIGH; Risk R1 probability = MEDIUM, impact = HIGH. Backend Developer allocation assumes standard API scope.

open_questions.question: Who is the designated Product Owner with explicit authority for backlog prioritization and trade-off decisions during Phase 2–3 sprints? What is their availability commitment (hours/week)?
open_questions.impact_if_unanswered: Hybrid SDLC requires clear PO authority. Absence of PO creates decision bottlenecks and delays sprint execution. Risk R5 probability = MEDIUM, impact = HIGH. PM role assumes PO function; if separate PO required, staffing plan must be revised.

open_questions.question: What is the data retention policy for onboarding documents and audit logs post-completion (e.g., 7 years for I-9 compliance, 3 years for audit logs)? Is this policy documented and approved by compliance/legal?
open_questions.impact_if_unanswered: If retention policy not defined, database schema and compliance controls may require re-architecture post-launch. Risk R10 probability = LOW, impact = HIGH. Backend Developer allocation assumes retention policy is defined in Phase 1 week 1.

pm_confidence_score.interpretation: PM confidence score is 68.0 because the project has HIGH input quality and a clear 26-week timeline with defined phases, but is constrained by 6 CRITICAL risks (Workday/Azure AD/e-signature integration, scope definition, PO authority, SOC 2 compliance, resource availability) and 3 HIGH-impact assumptions. The Hybrid SDLC approach adds adaptive sprint complexity. Confidence is further reduced by lack of pre-project stakeholder sign-off and undefined Product Owner authority. Mitigation of R1, R2, R3, R4, R5, R7, R8 in Phase 1 discovery (weeks 1–4) is essential to reduce risk score and increase confidence to 75+.

project_viability.gap_description: Critical path duration (130 days / 26 weeks) is 1.15× the deadline constraint (June 30, 2026 = 26 weeks from Jan 10, 2025). Project is at the boundary of deadline feasibility. Any Phase 1 discovery delay (vendor selection, API validation, compliance review) compresses Phase 2–3 timeline and increases execution risk.

scoping_options.title: Reduce Phase 2 feature scope to MVP-only
scoping_options.description: Defer 'nice to have' features (chat with HR bot, mobile app, LMS integration) to Phase 3 or post-launch. Reduce Phase 2 scope to: authentication, checklist, document upload, e-signature, Workday pre-population, Azure AD email provisioning (Slack/SaaS tools deferred). Saves ~40–60 hours in Phase 2, compresses timeline by 1–2 weeks.
scoping_options.impact: Reduces feature completeness at launch; may impact new hire satisfaction if Slack provisioning deferred. Mitigates schedule risk.

scoping_options.title: Augment Backend Developer capacity with contractor
scoping_options.description: Add 1 contractor Backend Developer at 50% allocation for Phase 2–3 (10 weeks) to accelerate Workday/Azure AD integration and error handling work. Contractor focuses on T11, T12, T17 (integration and retry logic). Estimated cost: $15,000–$25,000 (10 weeks × 50% × $300–$500/day).
scoping_options.impact: Increases project cost by $15k–$25k (total budget $80k; cost increase = 18.75–31.25%). Reduces schedule risk by 1–2 weeks. Requires contractor onboarding and knowledge transfer overhead.

scoping_options.title: Compress Phase 1 discovery to 2.5 weeks (vs. 3.5 weeks)
scoping_options.description: Accelerate e-signature vendor selection, Workday API validation, and Azure AD provisioning proof-of-concept by running activities in parallel (vs. sequential). Requires PM and Backend Developer to work at higher intensity in Phase 1 weeks 1–2. Saves 1 week, but increases Phase 1 execution risk.
scoping_options.impact: Reduces Phase 1 buffer and increases risk of discovery gaps (e.g., Workday API scope not fully validated). Mitigates schedule risk by 1 week but increases integration risk in Phase 2.
